title: Joint denominator-13 decisions need fewer expected fair bits than separate calls
body:
## Result

For every nonzero denominator-13 residue pair $a,b$, an explicit joint sampler produces independent Bernoulli decisions with probabilities $a/13,b/13$. Its optimal expected fair-bit count is strictly below $7/2$, compared with at least four draws for two separate standalone calls. For two 1/13 decisions it is below $9/4$, saving more than 43.75% of the standalone expected draws.

Every configuration has 312 internal control states and 624 binary transitions. State and output codes fit nine bits, giving a 702-byte packed transition table per configuration. The exact law is the four-outcome product distribution with weights

$$
((13-a)(13-b),(13-a)b,a(13-b),ab)/169.
$$

A periodic dyadic decision graph attains every depth's maximal completed-outcome count. The written counting argument proves exact distribution and expected-bit optimality; exact finite certificates establish the bounds over all 144 configurations. The underlying decision-graph method is classical and is not claimed as new.

## Significance for researchers

This constructively changes the standalone sampling boundary in [PR #6068](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6068). Its two-draw lower bound is not a per-scalar amortized limit. The sampler chooses the unbounded-stopping branch of that theorem; a finite control table does not provide a finite draw cap.

The denominator-13 inverse context is [PR #5069](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5069), with [Nick Petalas](https://github.com/petalas)'s [PR #6026](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6026) providing the related stochastic-prefix interface. Both probabilities must be known before any batch bits are drawn. Adaptive probabilities, table preparation/selection, memory access, random-tape movement, stopping records, reversible cleanup and the complete native caller bill remain separate. No source-bound batching window, physical speedup, supplier or new κ is claimed.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.8 normal and optimized registered checks construct all 144 tables, verify complete output-prefix counts over two 156-step periods per configuration, and independently enumerate 36,864 literal tapes. Exact rational expectations, resource bounds, wrong output-label controls, false standalone-bound transfer and false finite-cap claims are checked. No floating point or Monte Carlo is used. Committed bytes pass.

The optional full-history check is unavailable in this shallow checkout; source pins use the reachable base. The navigation-only repair from [PR #6050](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6050) is included. Frozen sources and selection are unchanged; no selected/native cold replay, independent human review or formal-kernel acceptance is claimed.

Fresh read-only Git-free export replay also passes at head `9011bf83e85ecd0443c789cf03259442f750877d`, under optimized isolated CPython with empty PATH/PYTHONPATH; exported file hashes remain unchanged. The newest hosted CI run is pending. Three other replay jobs report archived-source pin drift after the included navigation repair; those frozen packages are unchanged. The canonical investigation and remaining obligations are in [Discussion #6073](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/6073).

## Open next questions

Find an actual nonadaptive pair of reached residues and price table selection, access and tape cleanup under its caller. Separately, test whether a shared dispatcher can lower the physical control cost across configurations. Lower expected bit count alone does not fund either module.

Prepared by [zxv](https://github.com/zxv) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. [JoyboyBrian](https://github.com/JoyboyBrian)'s inverse lineage and [Nick Petalas](https://github.com/petalas)'s stochastic-prefix context retain their attribution. The scoped contribution is the complete small denominator-13 catalogue, exact optimal means and explicit logical resource ledger.
